newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-ITALY TAKE SHOCK 2-0 LEAD OVER SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ITALY TAKE SHOCK 2-0 LEAD OVER SPAIN.

text.p: Italy, virtually written off even by their captain, took a 2-0 lead over Spain on the first day of their Davis Cup world group quarter-final tie on Friday.

After veteran Omar Camporese, ranked 156th in the world, pulled off a remarkable comeback to beat world number eight Carlos Moya 6-7 (8-10) 6-7 (4-7) 6-1 6-3 6-3, Renzo Furlan gave Italy another five set victory in the second match.
Furlan, ranked 64th, defeated world number 12 Alberto Costa 4-6 6-3 4-6 6-4 6-1.
Australia led the Czech Republic 2-0, Sweden and South Africa were level 1-1 and the United States were playing the Netherlands in California in the other quarter-final ties.

Considering that Italian non-playing captain Adriano Panatta had joined in the chorus who gave Italy no more than a 20 percent chance of winning the tie, it was an astonishing display by the home side.
Camporese, 29, was the revelation after showing visible signs of pressure in the first set tie-break against Moya when he wasted two set points, the first on a lame double fault.
After Moya won the second tie-break, he felt he would win handily. "But after the fourth I began to think I'd lose. Things happen that way in the Davis Cup," the Spaniard said.
The beaten finalist at this year's Australian Open never showed the tennis he is capable of.
At the start of the third set Camporese gestured to the crowd for more support and won it 6-1, scoring the first service break by either player after two hours and three minutes.
His confidence high, Camporese then repeatedly hit the baseline with his drives as he raced through the final two sets against a lacklustre Moya.
"I had nothing to lose," a tearful Camporese said. "In front of me I had the world number eight. He had things to worry about."

Panatta's comment in the run-up to the tie that "they have an 80 per cent chance of winning, we have 20 per cent. That seems a realistic forecast," may haunt the Spaniards, who must win Saturday's doubles top stay alive.

In Vaxjo, Sweden, South African number one Wayne Ferreira lived up to his local nickname of "Swede killer" by beating Jonas Bjorkman 6-3 6-4 2-6 7-6 (7-3) to draw his country level 1-1 in their quarter-final.
Ferreira had to withstand determined resistance in the third and fourth sets before claiming his ninth victory in 10 meetings with the three members of the Swedish squad.
It was the world number 10's sixth win over Bjorkman and his only loss to one of the three Swedes here was to Nicklas Kulti.
He has also beaten Enqvist twice and will face him again in what could be a crucial reverse singles match on Sunday.
His victory over Bjorkman squared the tie after Sweden had taken a 1-0 lead on Thomas Enqvist's victory over Grant Stafford 7-5 2-6 6-4 6-1.
Bjorkman and Kulti face David Adams and Ellis Ferreira in Saturday's doubles. The winners of the tie will face Italy or Spain in the semifinals in September.
Ferreira began confidently against Bjorkman after saying he was playing his best tennis for months and won a textbook first set after the only service break in the sixth game.
The Swede changed his game and though he could not save the second set, his more aggressive play earned him an easy run through the third. But Ferreira remained calm and won convincingly.
"I was playing extremely well in the first and second sets but he played exceptionally well in the third and fourth," Ferreira said.
"But when I lose my serve I still have to be composed and focused and realise I can catch him in the next game and I did that.
In Adelaide, Australia took a commanding 2-0 lead over the Czech Republic after the Czechs lost a player due to illness.
Pat Rafter and Mark Philippoussis both won in four sets against lower-ranked opponents on the grass centre court at Memorial Drive.

With world number one pairing of Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde to contest the doubles rubber on Saturday, Australia looked set to secure a winning 3-0 lead and a semifinal meeting with either the United States or the Netherlands.

The Czechs, already weakened by the absence of four top players, suffered a setback before the start of play on Friday when Jiri Novak was forced to withdraw from his clash with Philippoussis because of a virus.
His late replacement, lowly-ranked left-hander David Rikl, proved no match for the big-serving Philippoussis and was beaten 6-1 6-4 2-6 6-4 in a match lasting one hour and 47 minutes.
Rafter earlier claimed the opening rubber by beating Martin Damm 6-1 7-6 (9-7) 4-6 6-4.
The Czech Republic's campaign has been hit by the refusal of Petr Korda, Daniel Vacek, Bohdan Ulihrach and Slava Dosedel to play in the tie.
